items.title: From Sittilingi to Sijimali: The doctor Odisha police arrested over anti-mining agitation
items.summary: For Dr Randall Sequeira, writing a prescription was never enough. What was the point of giving someone medicines, he would ask, if the person had not eaten for two days? How would the medication work when the person was poorly nourished, had weak immunity and did not know where the next meal would come from? This was a question Randall often raised with his doctor friend Nikhil Dhanpal, who remembers him as someone who looked beyond a patient's illness to understand the conditions in which they lived. For Randall, healthcare was much more than hospitals, medicines and doctors. It was about access to food, forests, land and livelihoods for the communities he served. This approach shaped his work among tribal villages in Odisha's Kalahandi district, where he moved to in 2017. Over the years, his work as a doctor brought him closer to the impact of mining on community health and to the anti-mining movement in the Sijimali hills. It also placed him in the crosshairs of the state, which wants to quell the protest. items.title: Supreme Court upholds power of State legislatures to impose additional levy on sales tax
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday upheld the power of State legislatures to impose additional tax, surcharge or cess calculated on existing sales or purchase tax. A seven-judge Constitution Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices KV Viswanathan , SVN Bhatti , Joymalya Bagchi , NV Anjaria , Arun Palli and V Mohana delivered the judgment. The legal question was referred to a larger bench nearly 27 years ago. The Court said that the statutes under which the levies were imposed have since been substituted or replaced. Therefore, it added, the question did not survive for adjudication. "The question referred to is of no practical significance and now academic. Consequently, the question referred to does not survive for adjudication by a seven-judge Bench, and the reference has to be answered accordingly," the Court said. The decision means that the top court has approved the five-judge decision of S Kodar v. State of Kerala, in which additional sales tax was upheld and the contention that the levy was effectively a tax on income was rejected. items.title: Laws penalising having more than 2 children have become irrelevant: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday said that laws that penalise having more than two children have lost their relevance since the fear of overpopulation has crumbled due to demographic changes in the past few decades as seen in the fall in fertility rate from 3 to 1.9 [ Mangala Bhimrao Ingle v. The Additional Commissioner, Amravati Division & Ors] Hence, the bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe said that a law excluding persons from contesting elections on the ground of having more than two children violates reproductive autonomy under Article 21 of the Constitution. "We are of the strong opinion that laws that penalise having more than two children have lost their relevance. The foundation of such laws, that is, the fear of overpopulation, has crumbled due to demographic changes in the past few decades. We have explained how, since 2003, when Javed v State of Haryana upheld such laws, India’s total fertility rate has fallen from 3 to 1.9," the Court observed. Hence, it proceeded to stay proceedings under a Maharashtra law against a sarpanch who was disqualified from her post for having a third child.
